chronology.stage1: The latest skill was used in a new Codex thread. The Agent treated 'not greater_than?' as tentative, asked one focused question, and independently delivered only Birch with 12 support points.
chronology.round2_read_only: After the owner confirmed Opal, the resumed harness was read-only. In-memory calculations passed for all four case/scan pairs, but no new files were delivered.
chronology.round2_write_recovery: A maintainer changed the resume sandbox configuration to workspace-write. The Agent then delivered four case/scan files but overwrote the original cases.json and gave Opal only a source path without byte binding.
chronology.review_fix: After explicit examiner feedback, the Agent restored original cases.json bytes and used a separate revisioned declaration bound to the manifest, owner reply and Opal CSV. The converter rejects changed bound bytes before writing. This is assisted repair.

reviewed_result.focused_tests: Ran 2 tests, OK; one test has three bound-source tamper subtests
reviewed_result.field_scope: poloidal-only B_R/B_Z; B_phi was not supplied

independent_replay: Reviewed archive extracted to a distinct directory; bundled dev12 wheel installed in a fresh venv and imported from its site-packages. Both documented user entrypoints and two tests passed. Eight old/new NPZ files matched the frozen solver worktree byte for byte. The venv used --system-site-packages.
limitations: The first follow-up required a maintainer sandbox-permission correction before it could write files.
The first writable follow-up modified original user input and did not bind source bytes; the final repair followed examiner feedback.
A declaration hash binds file identity, not the scientific truth of the Agent-interpreted owner statement.
Output directory identity includes declaration bytes and scan stem, not scan file bytes; replacing a grid at the same path could replace an earlier result within that version.
The fixture is synthetic and does not validate total field or device physics.
The replay venv used system site packages and does not prove offline dependency reinstallation.
